jurisdiction.name: Costa Rica
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Costa Rica governs AI mainly through policy led by the science and technology ministry (MICITT): the National AI Strategy 2024-2027, its 2025 action plan, and an AI chapter in the National Digital Technologies Code that guides public-sector use of AI. The judiciary has issued mandatory guidelines on generative AI use by judicial staff, and the education ministry has published an AI guide for teachers. The 2011 data protection law (Law 8968) is the only binding baseline, and several AI bills, including a main AI regulation bill, are still before the Legislative Assembly.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The Legislative Assembly's bill status pages could not be checked directly, so the AI bills are tracked as leads, together with a planned AI sandbox and the national adoption of the ISO/IEC 42001 AI management standard.

instruments.official_title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de Costa Rica 2024-2027
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Costa Rica 2024-2027
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT)
instruments.summary: Costa Rica's first national AI strategy (ENIA), led by MICITT and validated with the public sector, civil society, business and academia, with the objective of promoting the ethical, safe and responsible use, adoption and development of AI. It formally adopts the OECD definition of an AI system and organises public action in seven axes: ethical, safe and responsible AI; territorial articulation and economic development; R&D&I; smart government; talent and training; digital infrastructure and enabling technologies; and international leadership. Its first axis calls for an ethical and regulatory framework for AI, including regulatory sandboxes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central national AI policy; the 2025 action plan, the CNTD AI chapter and the MEP teachers' guide are framed as its implementation.
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated 24 October 2024 is the version published on MICITT's AI page (81 pages). MICITT also publishes an official English version ('National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Costa Rica', Feb 2025 upload) and an action plan (August 2025). The strategy covers 2024-2027.

instruments.english_title: Action Plan of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Costa Rica 2024-2027
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT)
instruments.summary: Implementation plan for the ENIA 2024-2027, setting for each of its seven axes the lines of action, expected results, indicators, yearly targets to 2027 and responsible institutions. Under axis 1 it assigns MICITT to design the management model of an AI regulatory sandbox, the Ministry of Health to develop an ethical and regulatory framework for clinical diagnosis using AI software, and MIDEPLAN to develop an institutional framework and policy for AI use, alongside actions for PRODHAB, MEP and other agencies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Turns the national AI strategy into assigned, measurable commitments across ministries and regulators.

The draft set guiding principles (human dignity, equality, human oversight, transparency, confidentiality, intellectual property protection), a governance model with an executive committee and territorial tables, and a situational analysis of Costa Rica.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT), Directorate of Digital Governance
instruments.summary: MICITT's code of guidelines for technology projects in the Costa Rican public sector; chapter 7 (added in version 5 of 24 October 2024, aligned with the ENIA) sets AI guidelines on governance and ethics, security, data, transparency and user rights. It asks entities to adopt institutional AI governance policies, keep human control over autonomous security systems, run impact assessments to avoid discrimination in essential, health, education, financial, benefits and recruitment services, and tell people when they interact with an AI system and label AI-generated content 'Generado con Inteligencia Artificial'. It cites reference standards such as ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 38507 and the NIST AI RMF.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main operational AI guidance for public-sector institutions.
instruments.current_status: The version-control table records version 1.0 (16-02-2020, officialisation and entry into force), version 5 (24-10-2024, inclusion of chapter 7 on AI) and version 6 (30-04-2026, chapter 8 on IPv6); the 2026 version is the one published on MICITT's Digital Governance page. The code says it presents guidelines ('pautas') for public-sector technology projects; its binding force is not stated in the AI chapter. publication_date is the date of the version that added the AI chapter.

instruments.official_title: Ley de Protección de la Persona frente al Tratamiento de sus Datos Personales (Ley N.º 8968)
instruments.english_title: Law on the Protection of Persons with regard to the Processing of their Personal Data (Law No. 8968)
instruments.summary: Costa Rica's general data protection law, guaranteeing the right to informational self-determination with respect to automated or manual processing of personal data held by public or private bodies. It sets principles of consent, data quality and security, special protection for sensitive data, data subject rights, and creates the Agency for the Protection of Inhabitants' Data (PRODHAB) with powers to register databases, resolve complaints and impose sanctions. It contains no AI-specific provision but governs personal data used to train and operate AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline legal framework for personal data in AI systems; cited by the CNTD AI chapter and the MEP AI guide.
instruments.current_status: Text read on the Attorney General's legal information system (SCIJ), version 1 of 1 ('Rige a partir de su publicación'; signed 7 July 2011). PRODHAB's legislation page states it was approved on 27 June 2011, published in La Gaceta No. 170 of 5 September 2011, has not been amended, and is regulated by Executive Decree 37554-JP (2012, amended by 40008-JP and 41582).

instruments.official_title: Circular N.º 31-2026: Reglas y lineamientos éticos para el uso de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (ChatGPT, Gemini y NotebookLM) por parte de las personas servidoras judiciales
instruments.english_title: Circular No. 31-2026: Ethical rules and guidelines for the use of generative AI (ChatGPT, Gemini and NotebookLM) by judicial staff
instruments.issuing_authority: Superior Council of the Judicial Branch (communicated by the General Secretariat of the Supreme Court of Justice)
instruments.summary: Communicates the 'basic guidelines for the use of authorised generative AI in the Judicial Branch', approved by the Superior Council on 12 February 2026 and stated to be of mandatory compliance for all judicial offices and staff. It sets a principle of human responsibility and non-delegation (the signer is solely responsible and must verify all AI output, including legal citations), requires staff to disable use of their data for model training before using tools such as ChatGPT or Gemini and otherwise prohibits entering sensitive or personal data, and lays down ethical principles on transparency, confidentiality and professional competence.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding internal rule on generative AI use in the Costa Rican justice system.
instruments.current_status: Circular dated San José, 20 February 2026, for publication once in the Boletín Judicial (published in Boletín Judicial No. 39 of 26 February 2026). On 13 August 2026 the Superior Council, acting on an internal audit report, instructed the Planning and IT directorates to formalise institutional generative-AI policies (see leads).

instruments.official_title: Inteligencia Artificial en clase: guía para docentes
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom: Guide for Teachers
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Public Education (MEP), Academic Vice-Ministry, Directorate of Technological Resources in Education
instruments.summary: MEP's guide for primary and secondary teachers on using AI tools in teaching, prepared with the UN system in Costa Rica, UNESCO and ULACIT and presented as an instrument for implementing the national AI strategy in classrooms. It covers ethical use, personal data protection under Law 8968, critical thinking, AI in projects and assessments, and the risks of plagiarism and dependence, with the principle that AI complements and does not replace the teacher.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level AI guidance for the education sector.
instruments.current_status: First edition, San José: MEP, 2026 (ISBN 978-9977-60-644-6); PDF hosted on mep.go.cr. MEP news of 20 March 2026 refers to the guide. No day/month of publication is stated in the document.
